key_insight: The paper proposes the Neural Health Index (NHI), a single score that summarizes resting-brain energy organization across EEG, MEG, and fMRI as a modality-invariant marker of neural health.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, NHI could help distinguish healthy from clinical brain states, track disease severity, and monitor treatment response across diverse disorders.
method: Modeled resting-brain signal energy patterns using five properties: lognormality, balanced spatial allocation, regional independence, low variance, and temporal stability.
Compressed these properties into one composite Neural Health Index score.
Evaluated the index across EEG, MEG, and fMRI in participants spanning multiple neurological, psychiatric, neurodevelopmental, and neurodegenerative conditions.
evidence_signal: In 808 participants, NHI reportedly separated healthy from clinical groups with sensitivity and specificity above 95% in internal and external validation, and generalized to unseen diagnoses.
watch_item: The abstract claims strong performance, but real-world use will depend on independent replication, standardized acquisition/preprocessing, and testing across broader sites and populations.
paper_title: A Modality-Invariant Measure of Neural Health
